To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relative importance of task performance, citizenship behavior, and counterproductive work behavior to ratings of global job performance depends on the individual rater.
(a) the relative importance of the 3 performance dimensions varies across raters, and (b) the relative importance is related to the raters' policies, but not their demographics.

the importance of task, counterproductive, and citizenship performance to overall job performance ratings varies across raters, and that the variation in importance can be categorized into 3 groups of raters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relative importance of the 3 components of job performance and the extent to which these components are weighted by raters.
how raters use task, citizenship, or counterproductive performance to evaluate overall performance.
the relative importance of the three components to ratings of global performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the relative importance of the 3 performance dimensions varies across raters, but the most common weight given to task performance is higher than the weights given to citizenship and counterproductive performance.
the relative importance of the 3 performance dimensions depends on the job, the rater, and the situation.
the relative importance of the 3 performance domains depends on the rater.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
task, citizenship, counterproductive performance, and global ratings of performance are not interchangeable and should be measured and evaluated separately.
raters use different policies in evaluating performance and that the policies used by managers are not related to their demographic characteristics.
the relative weights given to task, citizenship, counterproductive performance, and overall performance varied across raters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
raters differ in their weighting of performance components.
the weights that raters give to the different performance components are heterogeneous.
there is no one-size-fits-all approach to evaluating performance.
